entries.title: I Samuel 9:2
segments:
A choice young man; these words relate chiefly to his personal appearance. 
 
A sound mind and a well-formed, healthy, and vigorous body are rich gifts of God, which lay those who possess them under peculiar obligations of distinguished usefulness in his service.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:3
segments: All earthly possessions are liable to be lost; and this should lead us to seek those treasures which will be secure, and which when obtained will be enjoyed for ever.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:5
segments: As property is of little value compared with life, it is foolish, as well as wicked, for the sake of obtaining the one to sacrifice the other.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:6
segments:
In this city; it has been commonly assumed that this was Ramah, the home of Samuel.  But Saul, on his return home, passed by Rachel's sepulchre, which was south of Jerusalem near Beth-lehem.  This circumstance has led some to suppose that the city where Saul and his servant found Samuel was not Ramah, but some place near Beth-lehem, whither he had gone in the discharge of his public duties. 
 
If men were as anxious to be saved from sin as they are to find lost property, they would seek all needful information, and when they learned the way would let nothing hinder them from walking in it.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:7
segments: A present; such as it was then, and in the East is now, customary to offer.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:12
segments:
Before you; in the city to which thy were going. 
 
  The high place; the eminence on which they offered sacrifices.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:13
segments:
They eat; that portion of the offering which was allowed them in the Levitical law. 
 
Those who eat, drink, and enjoy the good things of life without thanking God or imploring his blessing, act in this respect like atheists, and the language of their practice is, No God.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:15
segments: The Lord makes known to those who do his will many things of which others are ignorant, and which no one without obeying him will ever know.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:20
segments: While men in their actions seek one object, God often by them accomplishes another; and no one, when he performs any act, can tell what great results may be connected with it.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:22
segments: Those who are selected by God as rulers should, for their office' sake, receive all due honors, and when the will of God with regard to them is known, all should acquiesce in it.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:24
segments: Left; rather, reserved, in anticipation of Saul's coming.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:25
segments: The top of the house; a retired place, to which they often went for conversation.

entries.title: I Samuel 9:27
segments: Ministers should make known to rulers as well as others the will of God, and none are ever so exalted as not to be under sacred obligations in all things to obey it.
